title: Design a BGP export policy
license_review: BGP Labs MIT notice is fetched with its pinned prefix-filter topology. The task, cases, declarative schema and checker are authored by Ascend; they model policy semantics and do not reuse router software or upstream grading claims.
worker_review: Fixed stdlib-only data worker; no submitted code or paths. Python -I -S, empty temporary working directory, minimal environment, 2 CPU seconds, 128 MiB address space, no child processes, 16 descriptors, 32 KiB per output file, 5 second wall timeout; parent caps accepted output at 16 KiB. No persistent pool. This is not a general executable-code sandbox.
evidence_label: Submission tested (policy model), when synchronized to an Ascend server
objective: Permit only the assigned customer aggregate and its allowed subprefixes; reject route leaks while keeping legitimate advertisements.
instructions: Edit policy.json using the assigned /24 customer prefix in assignment.json or TASK.txt. Permit that /24 and all of its /25 and /26 subprefixes; deny every other IPv4 route, including /27 through /32, loopback, adjacent prefixes and the default route. The JSON object has version: 1, default: permit or deny, and rules: an array of at most 32 objects. Every rule has action: permit or deny, prefix: a canonical IPv4 CIDR string, min_prefix: an integer, and max_prefix: an integer. Lengths must satisfy the rule prefix length <= min_prefix <= max_prefix <= 32. Rules are evaluated in order; the first whose network contains the route and whose length range matches decides. The default applies when none match. check gives local feedback including a counterexample for a wrong policy. finish saves the single bounded policy and, when connected, submits it for independent server tests of all canonical IPv4 route prefixes. Only policy.json as a JSON object is submitted (64 KiB maximum); shell commands, router configurations, code and archives are not accepted. To practice on real routers next, see the separate BGP Labs prefix-filter plan.

measurements.scope: Actual pinned downloads and local prepare/check/stop/resume/export/finish/destroy/reconcile/cache lifecycle. Worker samples use correct policy and a 32-rule policy with route leaks. CPU and memory are measured inside each fresh data-only worker; no router software runs. Disk includes retained work in four disposable attempts, sampled every 5ms. Server assignment, HTTP sync, resource timeout and malformed-result handling are tested separately.
